baseline:
B
Probability is a measure of the likelihood of an event. A fair coin has two equally likely outcomes (heads or tails), making the probability of getting heads 1 out of 2, or 50%.

C
The roll of a die and the flip of a coin are independent events. The outcome of one has no influence on the probability or outcome of the other.

B
Conditional probability is used because the probability of the second event (drawing a red ball) is dependent on the outcome of the first event (drawing a blue ball), which has already occurred and changed the conditions.

B
Bayes' theorem is a formula used to update the probability of a hypothesis based on new evidence. It allows us to calculate P(A|B) (the probability of hypothesis A given evidence B) by using P(B|A) (the probability of evidence B given hypothesis A), effectively reversing the conditional probability.

B
This is the definition of statistical independence. If two events are independent, the occurrence of one event does not change the probability of the other event occurring, meaning the conditional probability P(A|B) is equal to the regular probability P(A).
